where: Section 2, the paragraph beginning 'Read the row by edge condition', and the figure tree
problem: The list of the nine edge conditions is not the nine cases of IS 456 Table 26. Two entries are the same case under two names: 'one short edge continuous' is the same panel as 'three edges discontinuous with one short edge continuous', and 'one long edge continuous' is the same panel as 'three edges discontinuous with one long edge continuous'. Because of this double counting, the genuinely distinct cases 'one short edge discontinuous' and 'one long edge discontinuous' are missing. The figure repeats the same duplicated nine nodes.
fix: List the nine distinct cases: (1) interior panel, all four edges continuous; (2) one short edge discontinuous; (3) one long edge discontinuous; (4) two adjacent edges discontinuous; (5) two short edges discontinuous; (6) two long edges discontinuous; (7) three edges discontinuous with one long edge continuous; (8) three edges discontinuous with one short edge continuous; (9) four edges discontinuous, that is all edges simply supported. Delete 'one short edge continuous' and 'one long edge continuous' as separate items, and change the corresponding tree nodes to 'one short edge discontinuous' and 'one long edge discontinuous'.

problem: The rows are out of order: 1.20, then 1.30, then the interpolated 1.25. A student reads the table top to bottom and expects increasing ly/lx, so the last row looks like a misprint. The table also does not name the edge case in its own header; the case is only stated in the sentence below it.
fix: Give the table a title row naming the case, 'two adjacent edges discontinuous', and order the rows 1.20, 1.25 (interpolated, marked as such), 1.30.

where: Section 3, torsion steel paragraph, and worked example step 9
problem: Only the full torsion steel for a corner where both edges are discontinuous is given. IS 456 also requires torsion reinforcement of half that amount at a corner bounded by edges over only one of which the slab is continuous. The worked example panel has two such corners, and the chapter never mentions them.
fix: Add: at a corner where only one of the two meeting edges is continuous, provide half the torsion steel, that is 0.375 times the steel for the maximum midspan moment, again in four layers over lx/5. In the example this is 0.5 x 180 = 90 mm²/m, provided for example as 8 mm @ 250 mm c/c top and bottom each way over 0.8 m at the two mixed corners.

where: Section 3 checks line and worked example step 10
problem: 'Vu = w lx/2 at the long edge' is used without saying it is conservative. The short-direction strip actually carries only wx ≈ 0.71w of the load (Section 1), so the real shear per metre at the long edge is about wx lx/2 = 18.1 kN/m, not 25.5 kN/m. A student may take w lx/2 as the true shear.
fix: Say that Vu = w lx/2 is a safe upper bound that assumes the whole load is carried in the short direction; the exact share is wx lx/2 with wx from the Rankine–Grashoff split. Keep the same check.
